text: When the depth is increased to 2 2 and a nonzero dropout layer is included, as in [ 2 ] , the issue occurs for even less dense graphs. To diagnose the effect of oversmoothing on the algorithm, we performed the following experiment. For each depth 1 1 and 2 2 , each dropout rate 0 and 0.1 0.1 , and each order in { 10 , 20 , … , 200 } \{10,20,\dots,200\} , we binary searched the values p ∈ { 0.10 , 0.11 , … , 1.00 } p\in\{0.10,0.11,\dots,1.00\} to find the smallest value p p for which the oversmoothing issue occurred when using Mod-GCN on an Erdős-Rényi graph G ​ ( n , p ) G(n,p) . Note that due to randomness, there is not necessarily an exact threshold on p p above which oversmoothing always occurs, but this experiment provides a good approximation for such a threshold. The results are shown in Figure 10 . For depth 1 1 , the issue only tends to occur in graphs with density very close to 1 1 , but for depth 2 2 , the issue occurs in much less dense graphs. There are some potential remedies to the oversmoothing issue. When the GNN depth was decreased to 0 , oversmoothing never occurred regardless of the order, dropout rate, and density.
